interest: This document provides valuable insight into the U.S. State Department's monitoring of Japanese overseas migration and state-sponsored emigration policy during the interwar period. It highlights the significant scale of Japanese migration to Brazil—recording that 50,000 settlers took advantage of Japanese government subsidies for travel expenses—which accelerated following restrictive immigration legislation in North America. Additionally, the docket entry serves as a useful archival index linking specific Brazilian emigration records to broader State Department files on Japanese migration under decimal number 894.56/67.
overview: This file (894.5632) consists of a single State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet concerning Japanese emigration to Brazil. It records a March 19, 1932 memorandum prepared by William V. Whittington of the Treaty Division regarding the Japanese government's system of subsidizing passage expenses to encourage overseas settlement. The entry notes that approximately 50,000 Japanese emigrants took advantage of this assistance to settle in Brazil, reports on the current status of that migration, and provides a cross-reference to general emigration file 894.56/67.

subfiles.about: A State Department List of Papers sheet cataloguing a 1932 memorandum regarding Japanese government subsidies for emigrants traveling to Brazil.
subfiles.summary: This single-page List of Papers docket sheet for decimal file 894.5632 indexes a memorandum dated March 19, 1932, written by William V. Whittington of the State Department's Treaty Division. The recorded memorandum examines the Japanese government's system of promoting emigration to Brazil through passage subsidies, noting that 50,000 individuals had taken advantage of the program to settle there. It reports on the contemporary status of this emigration flow and directs researchers to related materials in file 894.56/67.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Emigration from Japan to Brazil
